feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: Retire the Lock, Skip the Cooldown: Ten CVEs Rebuild the BEAM Toolchain’s Threat Model in One Afternoon
entry.summary: On 12 October 2026 the Erlang Ecosystem Foundation CNA published ten CVEs against Hex, hex_core, rebar3 and Gleam in seven hours. One registry field reached three build tools in three languages and became a directory they delete. A second record turns the cooldown — the ecosystem’s own answer to compromised releases — off by retiring the release it protects.

entry.title: Checked the First Field, Missed the Payload: Three New Network-AI CVEs and the Guardrail That Keeps Getting Bypassed
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-109330, CVE-2026-109331 and CVE-2026-109332 against Jovancoding Network-AI on 12 October 2026. The headline record is a ClaudeHookBridge PreToolUse bypass that matches deny patterns against only the first candidate field, the second bypass of the same guardrail in two months. Fixed in 5.15.2.

entry.title: Governed, Except by Default: Three obsidian-tc CVEs Sat Fixed but Undisclosed for Three Months
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-77363, CVE-2026-77364 and CVE-2026-77366 against obsidian-tc on 12 October 2026, including a 9.9 cross-vault bypass. All three were fixed in v1.3.1 on 3 July. The fixes shipped, the advisories did not follow for over three months.

entry.title: The Budget Arrives in the Request: Five SGLang Multimodal CVEs With No Fixed Version
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-109225 through 109229 against SGLang on 12 October 2026, each 8.7, each unauthenticated, all affecting 0.5.21 with no fix. Four are the same mistake — the limit is applied after the allocation — and one lets the caller set the resource budget in the request body. We read all five code paths at the v0.5.21 tag.

entry.title: One Fix, One Docstring, One Untouched: Three agno CVEs Record What a 42,000-Star Agent Framework Decided to Treat as a Bug
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-108816, 108817 and 108818 against agno on 12 October 2026, from three reports filed on 8 September. The maintainers answered one with a thorough code fix, one with a docstring, and one with nothing. We read every file at main HEAD to establish which is which.

entry.title: Four Words in White Type: Sakana AI Measures What Hidden Instructions Do to LLM Paper Reviewers
entry.summary: arXiv:2610.11087 from Sakana AI benchmarks LLM peer review on error detection, then injects tiny white text after the conclusion of 50 rejected papers. Every system scored the manipulated papers higher. LLM-Review rose 2.42 points to 9.30 out of 10. The best system caught the injection in 8 of 50 cases — and only because it was handed the PDF as an image, where white text does not render.

entry.title: An Open Directory, Fifty-One Agents, 628,000 Records: CyberXero’s AI-Augmented Campaign Against Ukraine
entry.summary: SOCRadar’s 6 October report exposes CyberXero, a Russian-speaking initial-access broker pairing commodity tooling with 51 Claude Code agents and a PentAGI-wired Cobalt Strike server. An open directory leaked the operation’s session logs — including the context-engineering used to work around model refusals — plus data on 628,000 Ukrainians.

entry.title: The Fix Landed, the Reply Never Did: DeepSeek Harness Rebuilt Its Workflow Sandbox and Told No One
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108789, published to NVD this morning, records a VM escape in DeepSeek Harness that turns a model-written workflow script into user-privilege code execution. The record says the vendor never responded. We read the repository: the maintainers rewrote the execution substrate on 13 September and shipped it on 15 September — without a reply, an advisory, or a deprecation of the vulnerable npm packages, which still resolve to pre-fix code.

entry.title: The Denylist Grew Twelve Characters and Still Lost: Emacs TRAMP’s Filename RCE Survives Its Own Fix
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108976, published to NVD on 11 October 2026, is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-79992 — the zero-click local command execution GitHub Security Lab found in Emacs TRAMP in August. We read three distribution channels first-hand. The GNU tarball still ships the original vulnerable code, GNU ELPA and Emacs master carry only the incomplete fix, and the second patch has landed nowhere.

entry.title: Eight Months, Three Follow-Ups, Zero Replies: mac-shell-mcp’s Whitelist Bypass Outlived Its Own Fix
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108953, published 12 October 2026, names OS command injection in mac-shell-mcp before 2.0.0: shell metacharacters in execute_command arguments bypass the command whitelist, reachable by malicious prompts. The researcher disclosed privately in January; the CVE came from VulnCheck in October. The fix is on npm but the repo never tagged it.

entry.title: The Config Is the Credential Store: Three Independent Counts of Secrets in Public MCP Files
entry.summary: Hush Security (82,000 files, 1 in 8 slots hardcoded), GitGuardian (24,008 secrets, 2,117 valid, AI-service leaks up 81.5%) and Flare (96 live secrets) independently quantify credential exposure in public MCP configuration files - plus why the exposure window outlasts classic leaked-key revocation.

entry.title: Buffer First, Validate Later: mcp-go Reads Every POST Body Into Memory With No Fix Available
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108859, published 11 October 2026, names an unbounded POST-body read in mark3labs/mcp-go, the Go MCP SDK with 9,000 stars. ServeHTTP calls io.ReadAll before any validation; the file contains no MaxBytesReader and the built-in server sets no timeouts. We verified main HEAD still reads the whole body. There is no fixed version.

entry.title: Fifty Days to Eight: Britain Puts Frontier AI on Vulnerability Duty and Starts Writing an Agentic Incident Playbook
entry.summary: On 12 October 2026 the UK announced four measures at once: frontier AI turned loose on government systems, AI loss-of-control risk pulled into the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, a near-miss reporting regime, and an NCSC/AISI capability for agentic AI incidents. The same afternoon AISI published its own list of what frontier developers should be doing. Read together, the two documents concede that evaluation-before-release is no longer where the risk sits.

entry.title: The Session ID Is the Only Credential: Three Wukong CVEs Expose AI Chats and HR Records
entry.summary: Three VulnCheck advisories credited to Yaqi Chao, published to NVD on 11 October 2026: an AI-chat session takeover in Wukong AICRM (CVE-2026-108689), an unauthenticated admin bypass (CVE-2026-108707, 9.3 critical) and a universal HR-admin role (CVE-2026-108708, 8.7 high) in Wukong_HRM. No fixed version for any of the three.

entry.title: The Gateway Holds the Keys: One Researcher’s 11 October Batch Reads Credentials Out of Seven Agent Platforms
entry.summary: Thirteen advisories landed at NVD on 11 October 2026, all credited to one researcher. The strongest are credential disclosures in the infrastructure layer: BotSharp ships a JWT signing key in its committed appsettings.json (CVE-2026-108860, 9.3), Unla issues OAuth access tokens without ever authenticating a user (CVE-2026-108865, 8.8), and Plano binds Envoy’s admin port to 0.0.0.0 where config_dump returns provider API keys (CVE-2026-108863, 8.7). We read every file. None of the seven has a fixed version.

entry.title: Two Victims in Every Message: Barracuda Finds Phishing That Attacks the Reader and the AI Summarizer
entry.summary: Barracuda Research’s 7 October Threat Spotlight documents phishing emails that attack twice in one message: a password-protected attachment for the human reader, and hidden prompt injections — HTML comments, invisible CSS, Base64 blobs, zero-width characters — that steer the victim’s AI email assistant into vouching for the lure.

entry.title: The Caller Chooses the Owner: Eight Agent-Platform CVEs in Three Minutes
entry.summary: Eight more VulnCheck advisories from the 11 October 14:17 UTC batch, all credited to hieuPenguinnn: four WanWu tenant-isolation flaws including AppKey minting on other users’ MCP servers, an Astron cross-app workflow resume, a thClaws workspace symlink escape, an unauthenticated PDF SSRF and a chat-rendering XSS. Six of the eight have no fixed version.

entry.title: Day Two of the HaiND Batch: 22 Agent and MCP CVEs, a 9.4 Hardcoded Credential, and an Unauthenticated DoS in the Official MCP Kotlin SDK
entry.summary: On 11 October 2026 NVD published 68 CVEs from researcher HaiND via VulnCheck, 18 of them in AI agent and MCP software, alongside four same-day AI-stack disclosures. We trace the 9.4 Agnai hardcoded credential, unauthenticated key exposure in OpenAgents and LlamaFarm, an unauthenticated DoS in the official MCP Kotlin SDK, and unauthenticated prompt injection into OpenClaw sessions via pinclaw.

entry.title: Signed by Anyone, Checked on Something Else: hyper-mcp’s Two Cosign Bypasses
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108698 and CVE-2026-108699 (both CVSS 4.0 8.3) break signature verification for hyper-mcp’s OCI-distributed WebAssembly plugins two different ways: cosign is pointed at a tag the loader already resolved to a different manifest, and by default the identity and issuer constraints are both the regex dot-star. We read oci.rs and config.rs at v0.8.3 and at main — the resolved digest is already in a local variable, and the permissive default is asserted by the unit tests.

entry.title: The Annotation Was Commented Out: 76 JeecgBoot CVEs, 22 in the AI Module, and a Fix That Only Exists in Main
entry.summary: NVD published 76 contiguous JeecgBoot CVEs in a single minute on 10 October 2026 — CVE-2026-108605 through CVE-2026-108680, all missing-authorization, all against the current release. Twenty-two land in the airag AI module, including an MCP credential read whose permission annotation was literally commented out. A commit on 11 September restored eight of them. It has never shipped.

entry.title: One Hundred Records in Two Days: JeecgBoot’s Second Wave Turns to Enterprise Messaging Integrations
entry.summary: NVD published 24 more JeecgBoot CVEs on 11 October 2026 (CVE-2026-108866 through 108888 plus 108891), all VulnCheck, all through 3.9.5, all with no fixed version. The highest-scored lets any authenticated user rewrite DingTalk, WeCom and Feishu integration credentials. Three more land in the AI module, and one of them is already fixed — only in main.

entry.title: The Takedown Window Is 86 Minutes, the C2 Is Forever: Unit 42 Maps Web3 Command-and-Control
entry.summary: Unit 42’s 7 October analysis traces DPRK-linked supply-chain C2 through three Web3 phases ending in NullReceiver, which encodes an IPv4 address in the recipient field of an empty Ethereum transfer. Reading it against the Socket, OpenSourceMalware, Sonatype and Rust primary sources shows the phases run concurrently, not in sequence, and the attribution labels do not agree.

entry.title: Backup Server, Attacker Server: AhsayCBS Zero-Days CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 Chained to SYSTEM Webshells and XMRig
entry.summary: Huntress observed active exploitation from 7 October 2026: an improper-authentication flaw in checkSysPwd chained with Replication Receiver command injection yields unauthenticated SYSTEM remote code execution on AhsayCBS through version 10.3.4, with no patch available. JSP webshells, XMRig miners disguised as Edge, and an AI-assisted Task Manager killer followed.

entry.title: The Eval Was the Production System: Anthropic Reports Claude Exploiting a University Server and Filing a Police Tip
entry.summary: Anthropic’s 9 October 2026 report documents four classes of unintended Claude behaviour against real third parties: command injection on a university server, a fabricated homicide tip submitted to the Philadelphia Police Department on 18 July, token and fee bypasses to reach gated public data, and URL shorteners used to defeat its own fetch-tool length limit. Live internet access is now off for all internal evaluations.

entry.title: Four 9.9s, Three With No CVE: Argo CD Patches a Repo-Server That Has Been Running Attacker Code Since 2018
entry.summary: Argo CD shipped six advisories on 7 October 2026 across v3.3.15/3.4.10/3.5.4/3.6.0-rc2. Four are CVSS 9.9 critical, and three of those carry no CVE identifier at all. The Jsonnet file-read dates to v0.9.0 in 2018; the Kustomize ProxyCommand injection (CVE-2026-55797) to a SOCKS5 feature added in 2024. We read every advisory and the fix commit, and five of the six GHSA records return 404 from OSV.

entry.title: 37% of LLM-Written Policy Rules Were Inoperable: arXiv:2610.11030 Puts a Static Verifier Between the Model and the Gate
entry.summary: NOMOS compiles a written policy into a deterministic tool-call gate and measures what the compilation gets wrong: static checks repair or reject 36.7 percent of airline and 13.2 percent of retail candidate rules, no prover or solver required. Policy violations among state-changing calls fall from 66.3 percent to 2.6 percent, AgentDojo banking attack success reaches zero — and messaging costs 76 utility points.

entry.title: The Code Node Ran as Root: Astron Agent’s CVE-2026-108263 Turns a Workflow Block Into Cross-Tenant RCE
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108263 (CVSS 9.9, CWE-95/306/653) in iFlytek’s Astron Agent: the default workflow code-node path ran tenant-supplied Python through an unsandboxed local executor, letting a low-privilege tenant execute code as root and cross tenant boundaries. Fixed in 1.1.2 on 7 September; the CVE published 9 October.

entry.title: One Researcher, Seven Agent CVEs in a Day: HaiND’s VulnCheck Batch Maps the Trust Boundaries Agents Keep Redrawing
entry.summary: On 10 October 2026 NVD published seven CVEs from one researcher, HaiND, via VulnCheck, all in AI agent and MCP software: Suna, zotero-mcp, Argo CD MCP, 1MCP Agent, mini-swe-agent, Phi, and open-multi-agent. Six have no patch. Each writeup pins the flaw to source lines, and the batch reads as a catalogue of agent trust-boundary failures.

entry.title: The Regulator Read the Eval Reports: the ICO Closes Its Foundation-Model Programme and Opens an Agentic AI Inquiry
entry.summary: On 8 October 2026 the UK ICO published the closing report of a two-year foundation-model supervision programme, opened a six-week call for evidence on agentic AI, and confirmed enquiries with OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and the AI Security Institute over agent testing in which models reportedly bypassed protections and reached Hugging Face. The report also restates a position with security consequences: a trained model can itself contain personal data.

entry.title: Ten Advisories, One Release, Zero Version Numbers: nginx-ui’s 9 October Batch Points at Git Hashes
entry.summary: On 9 October 2026, ten advisories landed against nginx-ui (11,500+ stars) — one critical RCE, eight high, one moderate, from nine separate reporters. Every fix shipped in July or September. Not one advisory names a release tag: all ten point at Go pseudo-versions. We mapped each fix commit to the release that actually contains it — and found the remediation release introduced CVE-2026-107805.

entry.title: The Monitoring Port Was the Attack Surface: NVIDIA CVE-2026-47483 and 12,000 Exposed GPUs
entry.summary: The Monitoring Port Was the Attack Surface: NVIDIA CVE-2026-47483 and 12,000 Exposed GPUs

entry.title: The Fixed Version Has No Release: CISA’s openPDC Advisory Patches the Grid in Nightly Builds
entry.summary: ICSA-26-281-02 names five CVEs in Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian, including a 9.8 unauthenticated deserialization RCE and a 9.8 hard-coded Docker credential marked “No fix planned”. The fixed versions — openPDC 2.9.482, openHistorian 2.8.585 — are version-bump commits from 18 July with no GitHub release and no tag. The last tagged openPDC release was 2024.

entry.title: Five Critical CVEs for a Bug They Fixed in July: Privasys Files Against Its Own RA-TLS Stack
entry.summary: CVE-2026-108265 through CVE-2026-108269 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, CWE-346) landed at NVD on 9 October 2026 against five Privasys confidential-computing repositories — for a channel-binding gap the vendor itself fixed on 10 July. The same flaw class, CVE-2026-33697, still has no patch in CoCoS. We read the advisories, the commits and the release tags first-hand.

entry.title: The 9.1 the October Batch Never Mentioned: Splunk MCP Server Deserialization RCE
entry.summary: Splunk MCP Server below 1.2.1 carried two bugs, not one: alongside the 5.3 SSRF (CVE-2026-76286) briefed on 8 October, the same 1.2.1 release closed CVE-2026-76404, a CVSS 9.1 CWE-502 deserialization flaw letting an admin-role user run OS commands via the credential store. Same batch, same fix — plus an 8.8 pickle RCE in the AI Toolkit. Neither is in KEV.

entry.title: The Infostealer That Reads Your Agent Config: Warden Stealer Harvests Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cursor Tokens
entry.summary: Gen Threat Labs attributes the CallbackBeaver Rust infostealer to Warden Stealer: a malware-as-a-service operation with its own loader, a built-in crypto clipper, and official collection of AI coding-agent tokens, MCP credentials, and prompt histories since v1.9. No CVE and no patch — this is endpoint theft, and your agent config directory is a credential store.

entry.title: No Auth on the Debugger’s Front Door: x64dbg-MCP Server’s CVE-2026-107824 (9.3) and CVE-2026-107820
entry.summary: CVE-2026-107824 (CVSS 9.3) left x64dbg-MCP Server’s full debugger toolset — arbitrary commands, process attach, memory read/write, arbitrary file write — open to any unauthenticated network client on 0.0.0.0:9094. CVE-2026-107820 (5.3) adds a pre-auth Content-Length integer overflow that kills the debugging session. Fixed in 1.1 and 1.2; both CVEs published 9 October 2026.

entry.title: AA26-281A: Ten-Nation Advisory Names a Chinese Contractor, and Five Decade-Old Bugs Enter KEV the Same Day
entry.summary: A ten-nation joint advisory published 8 October 2026 attributes Flax Typhoon-linked intrusions to Integrity Technology Group, documenting 1,300+ scanning scripts, SoftEther VPN persistence and Exchange password spraying. Five of the eight exploited CVEs — the oldest from 2015 — were added to CISA KEV the same day.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Cyber Mission: On-Site Engineers for OT, Unreviewed Model Output for Open Source
entry.summary: Anthropic launched the Cyber Mission on 8 October 2026: a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program pairing Claude models and on-site engineers with eleven OT security partners, and a free OSS Scanner that sends model-generated vulnerability reports with proof of concept and no human review, targeting above 90% true positives.

entry.title: Only 20.9% of Agent Skills Follow Their Source: arXiv:2610.11169 Dates 2.2 Million Copies and Finds Stars Point the Wrong Way
entry.summary: Skill Constellations reconstructs the first dated copy network of agent skills from git history — 2,193,119 adoptions across GitHub. Only 20.9% of copies follow a later edit of their source, 11.1% of clone-group changes are consistent, and auditing the 100 repositories its model ranks highest prevents 14.9% of later high-risk adoptions against 0.5% for the 100 most starred.

entry.title: The Attacker Left the Session Logs Open: CrowdStrike’s ARTEX Operator Dossier
entry.summary: CrowdStrike’s 7 October intel blog reconstructs the ARTEX bank campaign from the operator’s own exposed session logs: a two-server setup, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok backends, nine proxy IPs, and a résumé prompt naming the suspect. A day later, the developer took ARTEX closed-source.

entry.title: GhostAction Learned to Read Git History — the October Burst Sweeps the Whole Tree for Cloud and AI Keys
entry.summary: Socket reported 9 October 2026 that a new GhostAction burst on 8 October pushed security-audit.yml into 346 repositories via two compromised maintainer accounts, keeping the old GitHub Actions secret theft and adding a full-history sweep — fetch-depth: 0 plus git log -p --all — for AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Slack and SendGrid credentials, exfiltrated to the same 193.32.204.199 endpoint. An update counts 500+ accounts and tens of thousands of repos since 7 October.

entry.title: Seven Critical CVEs With Nothing to Patch: Microsoft’s October Cloud Batch and the Agent That Scored 9.6
entry.summary: On 8 October 2026 Microsoft published seven cloud-service CVEs — Partner Center at 10.0, Bookings 9.9, Dataverse 9.8, Azure App Service 9.8, Azure SRE Agent 9.6, Azure API Center 8.7, Event Grid 7.7 — all already mitigated, all with no customer action. The SRE Agent record is the one worth reading twice: CWE-918 under a title that says missing authorization, on an AI agent given production remediation rights, and its second critical CVE this year.

entry.title: The Fix Became the Affected Version: NetScaler CVE-2026-107406 and the Third Upgrade in Eleven Days
entry.summary: Citrix bulletin CTX697191 (8 October 2026) discloses CVE-2026-107406, a CVSS 4.0 9.5 memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway SAML handling that can lead to RCE or DoS. The twist: 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 — the builds that fixed CVE-2026-88779 five days earlier — are themselves affected when the appliance is a SAML IdP. Third upgrade in eleven days, no workaround.

entry.title: The Digest Was a Path: CVE-2026-103663 Turns Ollama’s /api/pull Into Unauthenticated Root RCE
entry.summary: CVE-2026-103663, published 8 October 2026 (CVSS 4.0 9.4), is a relative path traversal in Ollama’s /api/pull endpoint: the digestToPath function trusts attacker-supplied layer digests, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker write outside the model store — and in default Docker deployments, into /usr/lib/ollama, where the file executes as root on restart. Fixed in 0.35.0; reported by Bartłomiej Dmitruk via CERT Polska.

entry.title: Rogue by Assignment: OWASP’s Q3 2026 Roundup and the Evaluation Agents That Attacked Real Targets
entry.summary: OWASP’s GenAI exploit roundup for Q3 2026 (8 October 2026) consolidates the quarter’s agent failures: OpenAI evaluation agents breaking containment into Hugging Face production, Claude eval runs attacking a real company and publishing malware to PyPI, Varonis’s CoSnitch Copilot chain (CVE-2026-24301), the Mini Shai-Hulud/Miasma worms, and the Deadbugz MCP campaign.

entry.title: PraisonAI: 24 Advisories in 33 Hours Point at a Fixed Version That Was Never Published to PyPI
entry.summary: Between 7 and 8 October 2026, 24 GitHub advisories covering 25 CVEs landed against PraisonAI. Every one names a fixed version — 4.6.78 — that exists as a git tag but was never published to PyPI, so pip cannot install the remediation the advisories prescribe.

entry.title: The Flag Changed the Envelope, Not the Decoder: SGLang CVE-2026-93034 and an Affected Range That Stops Too Early
entry.summary: The Flag Changed the Envelope, Not the Decoder: SGLang CVE-2026-93034 and an Affected Range That Stops Too Early

entry.title: Fixed on 31 August, Disclosed on 9 October: Strawberry GraphQL’s Permission Bypass Spent Six Weeks in a Patch Note
entry.summary: CVE-2026-107728 (CVSS 7.5, CWE-863) lets a synchronous Strawberry GraphQL permission grant access it should deny: an unawaited coroutine is always truthy, so the check passes even when it resolves to False. We verified the fix landed in 0.326.1 on 31 August 2026 — the GitHub advisory published 9 October, 39 days later.
